correctness.rationale: For finite nonempty X, fixed robust regions r_i and arbitrary independent truth supersets v_i, the generated minimal Alexandrov topology has least open neighborhood U_r(x)={y:s(x)subseteq s(y)}. An exact interior int_{tau_r}(v_i)=r_i occurs iff every maximal signature block outside r_i contains a negative truth label, since the outside signature classes form a lower ideal. If any finer topology makes all r_i open and interiors exactly r_i, then minimal tau_r already does so by monotonicity of interior under refinement. The blocks are disjoint, yielding E(r)=prod_i 2^{n-|r_i|-sum_{B∈M_i}|B|} prod_{B∈M_i}(2^{|B|}-1), probability prod_{i,B}(1-2^{-|B|}), and sharp positive-budget multiplicities prod_{i,B}|B|. For f_i=int_{tau_r}(v_i), tau_f is contained in tau_r but each f_i is tau_f-open, forcing int_{tau_f}(v_i)=f_i in one step. Includes duplicate signatures, absent maximal blocks and empty intersections, and does not falsely assert original r_i stay open in tau_f. Independent exhaustive tiny finite checks passed.
residual_risks: Finite independent computations corroborate but do not prove the arbitrary-parameter theorem unless the stated finite universe was exhaustively enumerated.
